transcript.content: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Um... I came in today because I just can't stop feeling like everything that goes wrong is my fault. It's... I don't know, I just constantly feel like I'm a really bad employee right now, and a bad homeowner. It's just this heavy feeling that I actually deserve to lose everything I've worked so hard for, and I can't seem to shake it.
Have you experienced these feelings of worthlessness and self-blame before in your life, or is this the first time you have felt this way?

Um... no, I don't think so. I mean, I've had stressful days at work before, but... not this constant feeling of being completely worthless. I'm pretty sure this is the first time it's ever been like this.
How long have you been feeling this way?
It's been quite a while, actually. I'd say this depression and... just the overall loss of interest in everything has been with me for about two years and one month now.
During these past two years, have you ever felt so overwhelmed that you started to believe things that others might find unusual or impossible, or heard or saw things that weren't really there?

Um... yes, I have. During those same months when I was barely eating, sleeping really badly, and just feeling like a complete failure... I was also hearing a woman's voice. And I really started believing that people were watching me, just waiting for me to make mistakes with my house and my job.
Have you experienced any other distinct periods of time in your life where you felt this depressed and had these types of experiences, or has this been one continuous two-year stretch?

Well, it's really been more of one long stretch. Looking back at it, the low mood and... just that total loss of interest in things have been there for almost the whole time since this all started. I mean, there have been a few brief periods where I felt like I could function a little better and get through my day, but mostly, yeah, it's just been continuous.
During these past two years, have those voices and the belief that people were watching you been present consistently, or did they only occur during the most severe parts of your low mood?

Well, they haven't just been there when I was feeling my absolute worst. Like, there was a stretch of several weeks where... where the depression lifted a bit. My mood wasn't quite as heavy, and I was actually getting through my work days a lot more normally. But even then, I was still hearing that woman's voice coming from near the air vents. And I was still completely convinced that the mortgage company and my coworkers were monitoring everything I did. So, no, they didn't go away just because my mood got a little better.

During those times when your mood felt a little better and you were functioning more normally at work, was there ever a period of at least two weeks where you felt that your mood was relatively stable, yet you were still hearing that voice and believing you were being monitored?

Yes, definitely. Like I was just saying, there was that one stretch... I think it lasted a few weeks, actually. My mood wasn't nearly as heavy, and I was getting through my work days a lot more normally. I didn't feel so down. But even during those couple of weeks when I felt relatively okay, I was still hearing that woman's voice coming from near the air vents. And I was still completely convinced that the mortgage company and my coworkers were monitoring me. So, yeah, the voice and the beliefs were still there for at least a few weeks, even when my mood was pretty stable.

Looking back over these past two years, have those voices and the belief that you were being monitored been present for most of that time, or have there been long stretches of several months where you didn't experience those things at all?

No, there haven't really been any long stretches where they just went away. They've been pretty constant for most of that time. If I had to put a timeline on it, I'd say... the voices and those fears about being watched, they've been present for about a year and eight months now.

During these past two years, has there ever been a period where you felt unusually energetic, didn't need much sleep, or felt so 'up' or irritable that it was noticeably different from your usual self?

No, I haven't experienced anything like that. I've never had a time where I felt super energetic or like I didn't need to sleep. It's really just been the low moods, the voices, and feeling like I'm being watched. I haven't had any periods of feeling unusually 'up' or anything.
Have others ever told you that your speech is difficult to follow, or have you noticed that your own behavior or movements have become strange, rigid, or disorganized?

People haven't really said my speech is hard to follow, no. But... I guess I have noticed some weird things I do sometimes with my behavior. Like, there are times I'll realize I've just been pacing back and forth, walking the exact same path from the kitchen to the front door, over and over. And while I'm doing it, I'll be rubbing my thumb against my fingers, just... constantly. And I'll keep stopping to check the peephole, even though nothing has actually happened and nobody is there. It's just something I catch myself doing.
During the most severe periods of your depression, did you experience other symptoms like a complete loss of appetite, significant weight loss, or difficulty concentrating for at least two weeks?

Yeah, I definitely have. My appetite gets kind of all over the place, but mostly... I just end up skipping real meals during the day. I won't really think about eating, and then I'll realize my clothes are fitting a lot looser and that I’ve basically just been living on coffee, toast, and whatever is easiest to grab. And yeah, concentrating is really hard during those times, too.
Looking back at the entire two-year period, would you say that you spent more of that time feeling significantly depressed, or were the periods where you felt relatively okay more frequent?

Looking back... I'd say the low mood has been there for almost the whole time since this all started. The depression and just... losing interest in everything, that's definitely taken up the majority of those two years. There have been a few brief periods where things lifted a bit and I could function a little better, but mostly, yeah, it's been the low mood.

Crucially, the patient confirmed a period of at least two weeks where psychotic symptoms persisted despite an improvement in mood, fulfilling the diagnostic criteria for schizoaffective disorder, depressive type.

diagnostic_checklist.duration_verified: Symptoms have been present for approximately 2 years and 1 month, with psychotic symptoms present for 1 year and 8 months.
additional_requirements: Presence of psychotic symptoms for at least two weeks in the absence of a major mood episode confirmed
Absence of manic or hypomanic episodes confirmed
